# Chapter 11 secret-gate fixture. Not a credential.
#
# The value below is invented. It matches the shape of an AWS access key id so
# that a secret scanner recognises it, and it authenticates to nothing: no such
# account exists, and the key was never issued by anyone.
#
# This file is allowlisted by .gitleaks.toml at exactly this path. Copy it to
# testdata/security/fake.env on a disposable branch, as the chapter instructs,
# and the copy is not allowlisted - which is how the gate proves it works.
#
# Expected detector identity: gitleaks rule `aws-access-token`, verified against
# gitleaks v8.30.1. Record that identity in the Security Finding Review record
# for the failing run. If your run reports a different rule id, the scanner
# version has changed and the recorded identity needs re-establishing before the
# evidence means anything.
#
# The value is not arbitrary, and this is worth knowing before you edit it. A
# key of the right shape is not necessarily detected: gitleaks stopwords
# low-entropy and well-known strings, so AWS's own documented example key
# AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE is silently ignored, as was an earlier invented value
# here. A fixture nothing detects makes the whole lab pass while proving
# nothing. Re-verify after any change:
#   docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/repo" -w /repo zricethezav/gitleaks:latest \
#     dir testdata/security --no-banner

AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=AKIAZ7XQWV3MNPKL5RTY
